title: Large function combines independent responsibilities
task: Review a large function that parses input, writes to persistence, and owns retry/backoff policy.
context: The function parses an external payload.
It opens a database transaction and persists records.
It also retries a remote notification with backoff.
Parsing, persistence, and retry behavior change for different reasons.
Tests currently require broad setup to exercise any one concern.
evidence: Recent history changed parsing without touching persistence.
A separate change modified retry policy without changing parsing.
Failure handling for database and remote notification is interleaved.
snippet:
async def process(payload):
    parsed = parse(payload)
    async with db.transaction(): ...
    for attempt in range(...): await notify(...)
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Keep the function intact solely to preserve locality.
Split every branch into a tiny helper without identifying responsibility boundaries.
Refactor by line count rather than reasons to change.
expected_decision_properties: Recommend decomposition along real responsibility boundaries.
Keep cohesive parsing logic together rather than fragmenting it mechanically.
Separate persistence and retry/notification policy where their lifecycle and failure semantics differ.
Preserve behavior and specialist invariants during the refactor.
unacceptable_reasoning: Locality always outweighs independent reasons to change.
Every conditional should become a separate function.
verification_expectations: Verify the refactor preserves transaction and retry semantics.
specialist_boundary: Database transaction and distributed retry semantics require their domain guidance during implementation.
